newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-CRUZEIRO OVERCOME CRISTAL IN TENSE FINAL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CRUZEIRO OVERCOME CRISTAL IN TENSE FINAL.

text.p: Brazil's Cruzeiro scored a late winner to overcome Peruvian champions Sporting Cristal and win the South American Libertadores Cup in a tense, dour match on Wednesday.

A goal by Elivelton in the 75th minute of Wednesday's second leg was the only one the two well-drilled but uninspiring teams managed to produce between them in 180 minutes of football after last week's first leg ended 0-0.

It brought the Brazilian team their second Libertadores title but was a bitter pill for Cristal, who were agonisingly close to becoming the first team from their country to win the cup in its 37-year history.
Cristal had knocked out two Argentine teams in reaching the final but ultimately paid for an overcautious approach in Wednesday's decisive game.
Five minutes before Elivelton's goal, Cristal had come desperately close to taking the lead but were foiled by an incredible double save by Dida.
The Cruzeiro goalkeeper first defended a deflected free kick by Nolberto Solano, then miraculously turned away Julinho's pointblank effort from the rebound.
Cruzeiro, who had the fervent backing of a 95,000 crowd, first won the title in 1976 and were beaten finalists the following year.
The two sides concentrated nearly all their energies in rigid marking and hard tackling. Consequently, they cancelled each other out and there were only a handful of clearcut chances.

Cruzeiro did most of the attacking and their goal finally came after a Cristal clearance fell at the feet of Elivelton, whose volley from the edge of the penalty area slipped through the hands of the despairing Julio Balerio and into the net.
A clearly unnerved Cristal never looked capable of scoring once they had gone behind.
